D.D.1.(2) (through Dy.B and B.A for information)

I have pursued enquiries into the activities of the SEYMONCZYK-LACOUTRE message by all available means since I took over the conduct of this case some few months ago, but I have not been able to establish any evidence of espionage activities on the part of SEYMONCZYK and LACOUTRE since their arrival in this country.

I think therefore that the time has come when a decision should be reached, either (a) to intern SEYMONCZYK and LACOUTRE under article 12 (5a) of the Aliens Order 1920 on the evidence available respecting their previous activities, or (b) to discontinue the enquiries.

The enquiries have been complicated by the fact that since the early days of 1941, SEYMONCZYK and LACOUTRE have been occupying the same flat (106 Oakwood Court, London W.14) as Andre LABARTHIE, (the Editor of "La France Libre") and Mademo Theresa ORLOW and her son Alexander ORLOW.

One of the main problems in the case has been SEYMONCZYK's association with a man whom I have at last succeeded in identifying as Karl GROENL & Stanislas RZELLA (the subject of PF.46464). This man has been exchanging somewhat cryptic correspondence with SEYMONCZYK (see, for example, numbers 124d, 159a and 162b in PF.52095), and meeting him regularly in circumstances which were consistent with ulterior activities, but when I ultimately established this man's identity I found that he was an agent employed by S.O.2.!

As will be seen from 1846 in the file, I have had an interview with S.O.2, and they inform me that they have known GROENL for a number of years and have no reason to doubt his honesty.
